Breakfast briefing: Intelligent networks: Powering AI native infrastructure for next generation customer experience
M4
Breakfast and lunch briefings
Please note this session is by invitation only. You can express your interest in attending by registering here.
AI-native networks represent a fundamental shift in how digital infrastructure is designed, operated, and optimised. As telcos respond to the rapid growth of AI-driven workloads, edge intelligence, IoT, and seamless multi-cloud to enterprise connectivity, networks must become more adaptive, autonomous, and intelligent. This evolution underpins the delivery of ultra-low latency, high-bandwidth, and secure services demanded by both consumers and enterprises.
In this transformed environment, AI is embedded across every layer - from routing and security to orchestration and lifecycle management-enabling intent-driven, self-configuring networks that can predict, prevent, and resolve issues before users are impacted. However, this shift also introduces critical challenges around scalability, trust, governance, and workforce readiness. This fireside conversation brings together expert perspectives on how telcos can successfully navigate the AI-native transformation journey and unlock its full potential with intelligent networks.
Key session takeaways:
Understand how AI-native networks operate in practice
Explore how autonomous networks deliver better customer outcomes
Learn how to manage the scale and complexity of AI-driven infrastructure
Identify the risks and governance challenges of AI adoption
Plan for organisational and operational transformation

The rise of agentic commerce: Why CSPs need an operating system for phygital experiences
AI isn't improving commerce - it's breaking the model. The future of commerce will not be won by optimizing channels. It will be won by orchestrating the experience between them. This session lays out iQmetrix's path to an Intelligent Commerce Operating System and the foundations we are building it on today: a modular, cloud and AI-native platform; an orchestration layer spanning activation, retention, and engagement; digital app experiences unifying the consumer journey across channels; TM Forum ODA-aligned open APIs; and AI already in production across forecasting, scheduling, and assisted selling. Jason Raymer, Senior Vice President of Client Experience, iQmetrix

From confusion to clarity: How Telenet reduced customer effort and cut billing inquiries by more than 30%
Even in a digital-first world, and despite years of transformation, billing remains one of the most complex and friction-heavy moments in the customer journey, and a major driver of confusion, inbound calls and churn. Telenet will share how it is delivering customers an effortless, digital-first billing experience powered by building a data foundation that enables AI-driven experiences. The session explores why most billing transformations fail to address the real issue-complexity and lack of clarity in invoices-and how Telenet simplified the experience without disrupting core billing systems. It also highlights the results: fewer calls, lower costs, an improved customer experience, and AI capable of accurately explaining even highly complex charges
Johan Morel, VP Billing Experience, Telenet
Walter Neeft, CEO, Calvi

From systems to agents: Reimagining BSS with agentic AI
As CSPs face increasing pressure to launch faster, personalize at scale, and operate with far greater efficiency, incremental BSS modernization is no longer sufficient. This is where Agentic AI offers a path to faster Time-to-Market cycles, adaptive monetization and partner management, proactive customer experience and reduced operational overheads. Those who master this shift early will define the next generation of digital-native telecoms. This discussion explores how Agentic AI is transforming BSS from static, rule-bound systems into adaptive, autonomous, and decision-capable platforms. You will learn what it takes to move from automation to autonomy, while examining real-world use cases.
Mark O'Flaherty, Chief Engineer, Digital, BT Group

Autonomous networks are moving from vision decks to real transformation programs, but the real story is bigger than network automation alone. Operators are being forced to rethink the economics and architecture of critical national infrastructure in a world where AI, data, and cloud are reshaping how networks are built, funded, and run. Crucially, this shift marks the end of siloed infrastructure decisions. The next build cycle demands a unified strategy that integrates technical capability with a hard look at the long-term economics of national-scale architecture.
This invite-only roundtable brings together communication service providers and ecosystem partners to discuss what it really takes to build AI-native, autonomous networks in practice. We will move beyond isolated pilots to examine how to re-architect underlying compute, storage, and cloud platforms while shifting investment priorities, risk models, and the fundamental economic assumptions of the future.
The conversation will explore how to turn today's AI and automation initiatives into durable advantages in cost, resilience, and service continuity, grounded in real-world roadmaps, collaborative build models, and the industrialization required to move operators toward scaled Level-4/5 capabilities.

detail.full_title: The Loft: Autonomous Networks
detail.description:
You can't automate what you don't understand: Why semantic digital twins are now essential infrastructure.
Digital twins are becoming a foundational capability for autonomous networks, driven by a market shift toward AI-driven, resilient operations. This session explores why this inflection point is happening now and the challenges operators face in moving digital twins from concept to production. It also examines the growing role of cybersecurity in network operations and how digital twins seamlessly combine security, network, service context, and policies in day-to-day operations. Drawing on 17 years of experience delivering semantic digital twins in some of the world's most complex operator environments, we will share practical strategies to overcome these challenges. Explore further at our Catalyst - Security use cases for digital twins - with Vodafone and Telia.
Anne-Flore Agard, Head of Telecom at Capgemini Engineering, Capgemini
Wim te Niet, Senior Vice President of Global Sales, NumoData
12:45 - 13:15
Grounding the agent: Why agentic network operations start with data, not models.
Most AI-driven network automation deployments stall before achieving a fully closed loop not because the models are inadequate, but because the data layer they operate on was never designed for autonomous action. This session makes the case that agentic network operations is fundamentally a data architecture problem. Drawing on deployment patterns across Tier-1 operator environments, we identify four precise failure modes that block AI closed-loop execution: unresolvable state across conflicting OSS systems, broken causal chains between alarms and remediation paths, absent post-change verification loops, and temporal data skew - the often-overlooked problem of AI agents reasoning over composite snapshots assembled from systems with wildly different polling cycles and propagation delays. A practical four-stage insertion roadmap shows how operators can deliver measurable value within 90 days while building toward full domain autonomy and how reaching AN-4 unlocks the shift from connectivity provider to Operator-as-a-Service.
Siddhartha Dattagupta, Chief Technology Officer, AXON Networks

Even though Autonomous Networks are increasingly moving from pilots to production, operators still face uncertainty about where to invest, which capabilities deliver measurable ROI, and how to scale adoption efficiently. This session, we're pleased to launch the TM Forum AN Benchmarks Project.
